name: Pap (ogi) with plain moi moi
why: Beans are among the iron and zinc foods the national guideline lists. This moi moi has no egg or fish.
prep: Make the moi moi without egg or fish.

name: Boiled yam with ugu and tomato sauce
why: Dark green leafy vegetables such as ugu are listed as sources of iron, folate and vitamin A. Tomato adds another vegetable.

name: Boiled yam with vegetable egg sauce
why: Eggs are listed as a source of iron, zinc and vitamin A (egg yolk), and leafy vegetables add iron and folate.
prep: Cook the eggs until fully firm.

name: Oats with banana and milk
why: Milk and whole grains are listed among the zinc foods, and banana adds fruit.
prep: Use pasteurised or well boiled milk.

name: Oats with banana and groundnuts
why: Oats and banana add fibre and groundnuts add protein.

name: Whole wheat bread with scrambled egg and tomato
why: Eggs are listed as a source of iron and zinc, and whole wheat bread is a whole grain.
prep: Cook the eggs until fully firm.

name: Pap (ogi) with milk
why: Milk is among the foods listed for zinc and adds protein to a light, easy breakfast.
prep: Use pasteurised or well boiled milk.

name: Boiled sweet potato with vegetable sauce
why: Sweet potato adds fibre and the vegetable sauce adds vitamins.

name: Ripe pawpaw
why: Fresh fruit is one of the food groups the national guideline recommends in pregnancy.
prep: Choose fully ripe fruit only. Wash well and peel.

name: Orange or tangerine
why: A good source of vitamin C. Eat it with an iron-rich meal.
prep: Wash the fruit before peeling.

name: Watermelon slices
why: Fresh fruit is one of the food groups the national guideline recommends in pregnancy.
prep: Wash the skin before cutting.

name: Carrot and cucumber sticks
why: Carrots are named by the national guideline as a food rich in vitamin A.
prep: Wash the vegetables well before eating.

name: Roasted groundnuts and banana
why: Groundnuts add protein and banana adds fruit.

name: Boiled egg with cucumber
why: Eggs are listed as a source of iron and zinc.
prep: Boil the egg until fully firm.

name: Plain yoghurt with fruit
why: Dairy is listed among the zinc foods, and fruit adds variety.
prep: Choose plain, pasteurised yoghurt.

name: Stewed beans with boiled plantain and vegetables
why: Beans are among the iron and zinc foods the national guideline lists, and vegetables add folate.
prep: Cook beans until fully soft.

name: Yam and vegetable porridge
why: A filling meal with leafy vegetables, made without fish or meat.

name: Rice with sardine tomato sauce and vegetables
why: Fish is one of the animal foods the national guideline lists for pregnancy, and the sauce adds vegetables.
prep: Check the can label for other allergens.

name: Rice with tomato stew, grilled chicken and steamed vegetables
why: Poultry is named as a zinc source and meat supplies easily absorbed iron. Vegetables add folate.
prep: Cook chicken thoroughly until no pink remains.

name: Vegetable soup with fish and swallow
why: Dark green leafy vegetables are listed for iron, folate and vitamin A, and fish is an animal food the guideline lists.
prep: Use dark green leafy vegetables such as ugu. Cook the fish thoroughly.

name: Vegetable soup with beef and crayfish, and swallow
why: Beef supplies easily absorbed iron, beef and shellfish are named as zinc sources, and leafy vegetables add vitamin A and folate.
prep: Use dark green leafy vegetables such as ugu. Cook the beef and crayfish thoroughly.

name: Egusi soup with leafy vegetables and fish
why: Leafy vegetables are listed for iron, folate and vitamin A, and fish is an animal food the guideline lists.
prep: Cook fish thoroughly. Made without crayfish.

name: Jollof rice with plain moi moi and salad
why: Beans in the moi moi are among the iron and zinc foods listed, and the salad adds vegetables.
prep: Make the moi moi without egg or fish. Wash salad vegetables well.

name: Yam porridge with vegetables and fish
why: A one-pot meal with protein from fish and iron from leafy vegetables.
prep: Cook fish thoroughly.

name: Okra soup with fish and swallow
why: Okra adds vegetables and fibre and fish adds protein.
prep: Cook fish thoroughly. Made without crayfish.

name: Rice with soya chunks stew and vegetables
why: Soya chunks are a meat-free source of protein and iron.

name: Brown rice with stewed beans and steamed vegetables
why: Beans are among the iron and zinc foods listed, and brown rice is a whole grain.

name: Boiled yam with pork stew and steamed vegetables
why: Meat supplies easily absorbed iron and pork is named as a zinc source.
prep: Cook the pork until fully done with no pink inside.

name: Boiled orange-fleshed sweet potato with ugu sauce
why: Orange-fleshed sweet potato is a vitamin A biofortified crop promoted in Nigeria, and dark green leafy vegetables add iron and folate.
prep: Choose the orange-fleshed type where you can find it. Wash the vegetables well.

name: Okpa (Bambara nut pudding)
why: Bambara nuts are named by the national guideline as a zinc source, and legumes also supply iron.

name: Ripe mango
why: Mangoes are named by the national guideline as a food rich in vitamin A.
prep: Choose ripe fruit. Wash well before peeling.

name: Tiger nuts and dates
why: Tiger nuts and dates are both named by the national guideline as zinc sources.
prep: Wash and soak tiger nuts well before eating.

name: Bitter leaf soup with fish and swallow
why: Bitter leaf is named by the national guideline as a zinc source, and leafy vegetables also supply iron and folate.
prep: Wash the bitter leaf well. Cook the fish thoroughly.
